title: Le futur proche
subtitle: Near future: aller + infinitive
review: Imported from the old tense page. Texts and examples are the old ones; the level is a guess.
intro: Describes **immediate or near future actions**. Very common in everyday speech. Equivalent to English “*going to* do something”.

examples.en: I'm going to call my sister.

examples.fr: Je **vais voir** ce qu'il me reste.
examples.en: I'll see what I have left.
We are going to change that.
Watch out, it's going to fall!
The train is about to leave.

examples.fr: Elle **va dire** non, je le sens.
examples.en: She's going to say no, I can feel it.

blocks.label: Uncertainty / Possibility
blocks.title: predicting or wondering about what might happen

examples.fr: Je sais pas si ça **va marcher**.
examples.en: I don't know if it's going to work.
Do you think it's going to be enough?

examples.fr: Je me demande si ça **va aller**.
examples.en: I wonder if it’s going to be okay.

examples.fr: On verra comment ça **va se passer**.
examples.en: We’ll see how it’s going to go.
We’re going to eat at their place Saturday.
Are you going to come with us?

blocks.title: Notes
points: This is the **spoken future** in French — more natural than *futur simple* in everyday talk.
Works with **reflexive verbs**: Je **vais me lever** à 7h.

Negative: Place `ne` and `pas` around **aller**
→ Je **ne vais pas** sortir.

blocks.text: ce soir, demain, bientôt, tout à l’heure, dans une minute, la semaine prochaine, ce week-end, dans un instant, d’ici peu …

examples.fr: On **ne va plus** sortir avec eux.
examples.en: We're no longer going to go out with them.
Are you going to go out?

examples.fr: **Futur proche**: imminent or scheduled — *Je vais manger.*
